identity.title: An ALMA view of star formation efficiency suppression in early-type galaxies after gas-rich minor mergers
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present observations with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) of six ETGs, which have each recently undergone a gas-rich minor merger, as evidenced by their disturbed stellar morphologies.

question.value: Is the strongly suppressed star formation efficiency in ETGs after gas-rich minor mergers caused by dynamically unrelaxed molecular gas stabilizing against collapse?

evidence.quote: It is possible that star formation is suppressed due to the fact that the gas brought in by the minor merger is not dynamically relaxed.
We observed the $^{12}$CO(1–0) line in our six dust lane ETGs with ALMA, as part of programme 2015.1.00320.S.

findings_qualitative.value: Five of six galaxies show detached clouds, warps or asymmetries; only 2MASXJ1333 appears relaxed

evidence.quote: Only galaxy 2MASXJ1333 shows no sign of asymmetries.

claims.hypothesis: Gas from minor mergers is dynamically unrelaxed
claims.experiment: Resolved CO(1-0) imaging and kinematic modelling

evidence.quote: These asymmetries support the interpretation that the suppression of the SFE is caused by dynamical effects stabilizing the gas against gravitational collapse.

claims.result: Much lower Σ_SFR at fixed Σ_gas
claims.finding: Strong suppression vs spirals and relaxed ETGs

evidence.quote: these dust lane ETGs have much lower star formation surface densities than spiral galaxies and relaxed ETGs at fixed $\Sigma_\mathrm{gas}$
these values are similar to those found in local spiral galaxies and therefore do not provide much power to discriminate
We therefore disfavour the explanation that AGN feedback (or supernova feedback) could be responsible for the abnormally low SFEs.

limitations_admitted.value: Edge-on geometry gives degenerate, upper-limit velocity dispersions

evidence.quote: We therefore consider our values upper limits to the true velocity dispersion of the gas.
